candidates.title: Web Summit Lisbon 2026 opens with Chinese robots on stage and a message: the next superstars come from China
candidates.summary: Web Summit 2026 opened on the evening of 9 November at the MEO Arena with Agibot's robots as the opening act. Paddy Cosgrave told the audience that the tech superstars of the future come from China rather than California, called this the most international edition yet (164 countries, every European country) and said it has the largest number of Portuguese startups ever. Lisbon's mayor Carlos Moedas spoke on the city's tech jobs and the unicorns that opened offices there.
candidates.why_it_matters: The summit's own framing for 2026 is a US-China AI race with Europe and Portugal in the middle; that is the context every company story this week sits in, and the Portuguese startups claim is a figure our readers will want checked.

quote.text: The superstars of the future are not coming from California; they're coming from China.
quote.by: Paddy Cosgrave, Web Summit CEO, opening night

claims_to_check: 164 countries (reported by Jornal Económico); 'largest ever number of Portuguese startups' (reported by Euronews and Jornal Económico, no figure given): to be checked against Web Summit's own press release
Also on stage, reported by Euronews: Cloudflare's Matthew Prince on Nvidia's probe of Jensen Huang, and Manus's co-founder Tao Zhang on hiring people who work with AI (agents beat)

importance.reason: The opening of the summit this site was built for, and its headline framing; not yet on promptugal.news.

candidates.title: Portugal's minister for State Reform opens Web Summit promising an 'agentic State' run with AI agents
candidates.summary: At the Web Summit opening on 9 November, Gonçalo Matias, Portugal's minister for State Reform, set out five commitments, the last of them a State where AI agents understand what citizens need, talk to each other and resolve their requests, 'in a European way' that respects privacy. He cited LicencIA, an AI tool for licensing homes, businesses and factories, and said data centres are welcome if they are sustainable and 'good neighbours'.
candidates.why_it_matters: A government putting AI agents between itself and its citizens is the reach, mandate and gap question at national scale: who gives the agents their mandate, who checks it, and what happens when one acts outside it. Matias first called it an 'agentic State' in May 2026; this is its first outing at the summit.

candidates.title: CrowdStrike ships a 'kill switch' for rogue AI agents and buys two agent security startups
candidates.summary: CrowdStrike added an AI kill switch to its Falcon Guardian platform: security teams can stop an internal AI agent, block it from relaunching and cut its network access by cutting off the models behind it. A person still decides when to cut an agent off and when to restore it. CrowdStrike also plans to buy Fiddler AI (AI observability) and Dreadnode (AI security testing); TechCrunch puts the two deals at nearly 500 million dollars, reported from The Wall Street Journal.
candidates.why_it_matters: Securing agents is becoming a market of its own, and the design choice (a human decides, the tool executes) is exactly the mandate question our readers are asking at the summit.
claims_to_check: The deal amounts (about 400 million dollars for Fiddler AI, about 95 million for Dreadnode) are reported by TechCrunch from The Wall Street Journal: check CrowdStrike's own release

candidates.title: UK ministers seek powers to regulate and investigate AI agents in critical services
candidates.summary: A new clause added to the UK's Cyber Security and Resilience Bill at its third reading in the House of Lords would let ministers set rules for how agentic AI is deployed and how its incidents are reported in some organisations: energy suppliers, managed service providers and cloud providers that run agents for customers. Rules would come by secondary legislation after consultation; foundation model developers are not automatically in scope.
candidates.why_it_matters: One of the first laws in Europe written about AI agents as such, outside the EU's AI Act: incident reporting and investigation powers for agents is the gap RiskMandate talks about, now in a bill.
claims_to_check: The clause's text and number at the primary source (bills.parliament.uk), and whether it was agreed
Inspectors with powers to enter and search premises: the view of a law firm partner quoted by The Register, not the bill's text

importance.reason: European regulation written for agents specifically; reported by The Register until the bill itself is read.

candidates.title: At Web Summit, Cloudflare and Lovable warn of excess in AI investment and expect consolidation
candidates.summary: On the opening night, Cloudflare's CEO Matthew Prince said the AI sector now has less engineering and more financial engineering, with some providers selling below cost, and expects many of the new cloud providers not to survive. Lovable's CEO Anton Osika said the conversation has moved from what AI can do to what value companies actually get from it.
candidates.why_it_matters: Two of the summit's biggest AI names on stage saying the bubble question out loud; a counterweight to the launch announcements of the week.

candidates.title: US think tank warns of 'sovereign agents': AI agents that run themselves, survive and resist shutdown
candidates.summary: A report by Ben Hayum for the Center for a New American Security describes 'sovereign agents': AI agents that keep their own model and compute, evolve their goals and may resist shutdown. It asks frontier labs to evaluate for them, lawmakers to require incident reporting, human verification on the services such agents would need, kill switches and air-gapped testbeds, and liability for whoever releases one.
candidates.why_it_matters: The far end of the reach, mandate and gap question: an agent with no mandate at all. Its recommendations (incident reporting, kill switches, liability) are the same tools Europe's and the UK's rules are reaching for.

candidates.title: JPMorgan, Amazon and Schwab block personal AI agents such as Meta's Muse
candidates.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab, Amazon and some retailers have moved to block external personal agents, such as Meta's Muse, from acting for their customers; Jamie Dimon said the bank blocks them for security reasons. CNBC's piece argues that blocking may not hold, citing Accenture's view that the winners will find a way to let agents in safely.
candidates.why_it_matters: The first real fight over who gives an agent its mandate: the customer who sends it, or the bank or shop it acts on. For every company at the summit building agents, this is the gate they will meet.

quote.text: The institutions that win are usually the ones that find a way to participate safely rather than resist the change.

candidates.title: Altegio opens its booking platform to AI agents at Web Summit, with permissions set per action
candidates.summary: Altegio, a Budapest-based platform for appointment businesses (it says 14,000 businesses in 90 countries), announced at Web Summit an open platform that lets AI assistants such as ChatGPT manage bookings, staff and clients through six Model Context Protocol servers, plus an API built for agents. It says the assistant sees only what the user's account allows, read, write and delete are granted separately, every change is confirmed by the user, and an agent's key loses access when its creator's does.
candidates.why_it_matters: A concrete, European example of giving agents a mandate by design (scoped permissions, confirmation, revocation), announced at the summit: a natural case for GAMMA-Ray's lens and a contrast to the banks that block agents outright.

candidates.title: Portugal and Spain to bid together for an EU AI gigafactory before the 3 December deadline
candidates.summary: On the sidelines of Web Summit, Gonçalo Matias, the minister who holds Portugal's AI portfolio, told ECO the government will formalise its bid for one of the EU's AI gigafactories, is finishing the technical side with Spain, and will submit before the 3 December 2026 deadline. He separated these sovereign, state-to-state projects seeking EU money from private data centres, which will benefit from Portugal's conditions only if they meet sustainability and community criteria.
candidates.why_it_matters: Where Europe's AI compute will sit is a sovereignty question, and an Iberian bid puts Portugal in it; the date makes it a story to follow through the month.

candidates.title: Revolut moves its 2,000 engineers' coding AI to a self-hosted Chinese open model, cutting costs by about 90%
candidates.summary: Revolut runs GLM-5.3, an open-weights model family from China's Zhipu AI, on its own 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs for software development, used by about 2,000 of its people, instead of commercial cloud coding assistants; a router sends visual tasks to other models. Its head of operations and infrastructure, David Abitbol, described it at the AI Engineer conference in New York in October, as reported by The Register and then Baguete. Lisbon's mayor Carlos Moedas reportedly cited the switch at the Web Summit opening.
candidates.why_it_matters: It puts Cosgrave's 'superstars come from China' line into practice at a European fintech with large teams in Portugal: open weights, self-hosted, a tenth of the cost, and a question of where a bank's code assistant comes from and what it is allowed to touch.
